item.title: Review: The month’s best experimental album: Stella Z’s ambient adventures into lucid dreaming
item.description: (CDR) Based around sounds recorded on her trips back to China, the Fujian-born, London-based producer creates a curious nocturnal collage on Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming Lucid dreaming is one of the influences behind Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming, the new record from Fujian-born, London-based producer Stella Z. “Every night is an adventure,” she writes in the liner notes, “I can even smell things in certain dreams.” The eight tracks here are suitably sensory, scattered with effervescent sounds, ephemeral whispers and polyrhythmic percussion. item.description: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news Retail sales in Great Britain surged last month as the public rushed to buy products including tinned food and long-life milk, after the government issued a warning to stock up in case of a disaster. item.description: (EMI) The pallid disco revivalism sounds like S Club 7 and the folksy stomp-clap like Mumford and Sons – yet a few standout moments prove they can still strike gold if they try Listening to Wonderkids, the string-laden opener of Take That’s new album, it seems the three remaining fiftysomething boybanders are feeling reflective. “Forgiving you, forgiving me / This vicious circle is now complete,” sings Gary Barlow. item.title: Review: Joanne Young praised for bravery in exposing rape by husband and strangers
item.description: Woman who waived anonymity says she hopes her case will mean other victims of abuse are more likely to come forward A woman who was drugged and raped by her husband and strangers he had invited to their family home has been praised for her bravery in exposing the crimes. The judge in the case and women’s rights advocates said Joanne Young’s courage had been a feature of the trial. Her decision to waive her anonymity and attend court has drawn comparisons to Gisèle Pelicot, who was drugged and raped by her husband as well as dozens of strangers in France. Waiving her right to anonymity, Pelicot said shame “must change sides”. Continue reading...
